specName: One set of rules for every screen, window and dialog

FR-001.title: Every dialog opens as its own window owned by the main window

FR-002.title: A dialog stays centred on its owner while the owner moves or resizes

FR-003.title: A dialog never opens larger than its owner; its body scrolls instead

FR-004.title: A dialog declares a minimum and preferred width from the shared sizing values

FR-005.title: A dialog's title names the subject it acts on

FR-006.title: Message and question dialogs are windowed too, and come from the standard set

FR-007.title: A converted dialog keeps the visual styling it had

FR-008.title: One shared set covers every message kind: acknowledge, confirm, decide, destructive, leave, retry

FR-009.title: For each kind the action order, default action and cancel position are the same everywhere

FR-010.title: Message wording names the subject and the consequence of the default action

FR-011.title: A message dialog returns the same answer shape its callers already expect

FR-012.title: One shared entry point raises every message; no screen builds its own

FR-013.title: Every screen draws its content in one capped centred column

FR-014.title: Every screen uses the shared spacing scale

FR-015.title: Every screen takes its colours from the theme brushes

FR-016.title: Every screen takes its text sizes from the shared type scale

FR-017.title: Every screen adapts at the declared breakpoints without clipping

FR-018.title: Every operable control carries an accessible name and a stable identifier

FR-019.title: Automation identifiers are unique within a screen

FR-020.title: Every screen is operable by keyboard alone in reading order

FR-021.title: No XAML file or its code uses an API the api-rules instruction file forbids

FR-022.title: Named replacements are in use; navigation stays on the existing services

FR-023.title: One inventory lists every surface including the service console window and pages

FR-024.title: Every surface lives in its own file declaring exactly one type

FR-025.title: The inventory is checked automatically so it cannot go stale

FR-026.title: Every XAML file meets the rules with no exclusion list and no per-file exemption

FR-027.title: A surface that cannot meet the rules is rearranged, keeping its behaviour

FR-028.title: Every tooltip is declared through the shared tooltip behaviour

FR-029.title: New converters and resource dictionaries are registered in the same change

FR-030.title: A dialog awaits its own show call directly

FR-031.title: A diagnostic surface raised over a dialog is a window, not a page

FR-032.title: The standard message set lives in the shared layer all consumers reference

FR-033.title: A fragment control stays a control, and still meets the rules

FR-034.title: The mapping from today's raise sites to the six kinds is recorded

expectations: Flyouts and the picture enlarge overlay are not modal windows and are not converted
Flow behaviour, wording, gestures and return values are preserved, not redesigned
The three instruction files are the authority; this feature does not rewrite them
Screens are aligned and made consistent, not rebuilt
context: area: all 77 XAML files (Module_Core, Module_Startup, Module_Settings, Module_Setup, Module_Waitlist, Module_Shared, Module_Mock, MTM_Waitlist.Mock.Service, root, Styles)
constraint: winui3-adoption.instructions (spacing scale, type ramp, capped column, adaptive breakpoints, theme brushes)
constraint: winui3-api-rules.instructions (forbidden APIs and their named replacements)
constraint: winui3-ui-automation.instructions (accessible names, automation ids, keyboard reach, focus order)
measurement: 8 ContentDialog-rooted dialog files, 14 screens raising a ContentDialog in code, 1 dialog already windowed with DevWinUI.WindowedContentDialog
measurement: no XAML file declares more than one type, so no embedded-type split is needed
measurement: PageContentMaxWidth (1080) exists; 3 pages still carry a literal MaxWidth (720, 720, 960)
living spec: none configured for this project
measurement: 14 screens construct their own dialog; only 2 shared prompts exist (waitlist action prompt, setup dialog service)
measurement: no dialog in the application uses three actions, so the standard message set needs at most two
decision: message-only dialogs are windowed and come from one standard set of six kinds
decision: the service console (separate executable) is in scope: its window and both pages
decision: no exemptions - every XAML file is treated as a production page, including the control inspector, the developer log panel and the service console
decision: a surface that cannot meet the rules without rearrangement has its layout redesigned, with behaviour preserved

constraint: api rules also require the shared tooltip behaviour, resource registration in the same change, direct await of the dialog show call, and a window for a diagnostic surface raised over a dialog
clarify Q1: dialog sizing 480 min / 720 preferred / 880 max / 640 max body height / 120 body floor, chosen for a 15-inch screen at 150%
clarify Q2: raise-site to message-kind mapping established by reading the code
clarify Q3: standard set lives in MTM_Waitlist.Shared; DevWinUI added there; Mock.Service gains a project reference to it
clarify Q4: the developer log panel stays a control inside the Diagnostics page, not a surface
clarify Q5: the control inspector's fixed 172px column becomes proportional and its type moves onto the shared scale
intent: Bring every XAML surface, with no exemptions, onto one set of layout, sizing, automation and platform rules; move every dialog, message and question into its own window centred on the main window with one standard message set; redesign any layout that cannot comply.

decisions.why: Satisfies the request and the api rule that asks for ContentDialog; the repo already proves the pattern in LuggerEditorDialog
decisions.rejected: A hand-built Window with its own button bar, which would lose framework Escape and default-button handling

decisions.decision: Put the message set in MTM_Waitlist.Shared
decisions.why: It is the only project every module and the service console can reference, so one implementation serves all
decisions.rejected: MTM_Waitlist.Core, which holds no XAML, or a copy in the console

decisions.why: Fits a 15-inch screen at 150% and never outgrows the 1080 page column
decisions.rejected: Per-dialog literals, which is today's four different values, or deriving from the page column

decisions.decision: Six message kinds classified from the code
decisions.why: The code fixes the answer; Leave and Decide are separate because their defaults protect different things
decisions.rejected: One generic confirm with caller-supplied labels, which is what caused the inconsistency

decisions.why: The one surface that cannot fit a capped column at a fixed width; FR-027 authorises the redesign
decisions.rejected: Exempting it, or allowing horizontal scrolling

plan.summary: Plan, research, data model and the message-dialog contract written for an oversized change spanning 77 XAML files.
plan.key_finding: WindowedContentDialog is a host for ContentDialog content, so the request and the api rule agree; one shared set in Shared serves the app and the console.

approach: Build the shared pieces first: dialog sizing resources, a windowed dialog host, and one standard set of six message dialogs in MTM_Waitlist.Shared. Then convert every raise site to them, sweep the remaining surfaces for layout, tooltip and automation conformance, and add source audits that fail the build if any of it drifts.
